readings: Match each `player_college` record to its player by `player_id`, dropping records with no matching player. Count the matched college records (one per player-college-year row) for each `birth_country`, and work out each country's share of the total of those counts. Now take only the countries whose record count is above the average record count across all countries. In one row, give the total record count of those countries, their average share, and the average amount by which their record count exceeds that overall average. Don't round anything.
queries:
WITH country_counts AS (
    SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM player_college AS pc
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id
    GROUP BY p.birth_country
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) AS average_count,
           SUM(record_count) AS total_count
    FROM country_counts
)
SELECT SUM(c.record_count) AS total_record_count,
       AVG(c.record_count * 1.0 / o.total_count) AS average_share,
       AVG(c.record_count - o.average_count) AS average_excess
FROM country_counts AS c
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE c.record_count > o.average_count;
